A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. The complete main text and appendices are readable and matchable despite reorganization; all 11 figures and Table 1 are retained.

before.justification: V2 reports original recourse experiments, baseline comparisons, sensitivity analyses, and actionability tests in Section 4 and Appendix D.

after.justification: V3 retains these original experiments in Section 4 and Appendix C and additionally reports LIME-fidelity measurements.

M1.justification: Algorithm 2 changes its objective-improvement selection from argmin with positive-infinity initialization to argmax with negative-infinity initialization, revises the update condition, and explicitly receives the adversarial parameters. These correct the reported procedure without replacing the overall method; implementation changes or experimental reruns are not established.

E1.justification: Both versions use synthetic, German Credit, Small Business Administration, and ACSIncome-CA data with the same recourse tasks and shift scenarios. The fidelity analysis concerns existing models and instances.

E2.justification: The corresponding experiments retain the same ROAR variants and RBR comparisons. Full ROAR robustness-consistency curves and its modified smoothness baseline already appear in v2.

E3.justification: V3 adds evaluation of LIME approximation fidelity, averaged over instances receiving recourse, in Appendix C.6. The existing five-fold splits, model configurations, training budgets, and parameter grids remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix C.6 adds a diagnostic analysis relating LIME approximation quality to performance against RBR. The existing prediction-error, parameter-sensitivity, and actionability/post-processing analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report averages over folds and recourse instances and retain the same robustness and consistency error bars in Figures 4 and 5. No new seed information, repeated-run counts, or uncertainty procedures are reported.

E6.justification: V3 newly reports neural-network LIME fidelities of 0.93 for synthetic data, 0.54 for Small Business, and 0.02 for German Credit. It also corrects the stated RBR comparison to acknowledge the German neural-network exception. The plotted results and Table 1 values are unchanged.

T1.justification: Theorem 3.3 now explicitly assumes that Algorithm 2's single-dimensional convex optimization can be solved in polynomial time. The appendix optimality proof is retained; the new main-text proof sketch and Proposition B.1 largely restate existing arguments and the existing non-convexity example.

C1.justification: The abstract and central contribution claims remain the learning-augmented recourse framework, optimal robust and consistent recourse for generalized linear models, and empirical trade-off advantages over ROAR. The introduction's more cautious optimization wording does not introduce a different central contribution.

C2.justification: V3 interprets the German neural-network weakness in terms of very low LIME fidelity and acknowledges RBR's advantage, refining v2's broader dominance discussion. It also expands discussion of performative prediction and imperfect recourse implementation. The expanded algorithm explanation introduces a sign-condition inequality inconsistent with Algorithm 1.

D1.justification: Section 4 now supplies an explicit repository link and states that code and data are available; v2 refers to code without providing that access address. Existing hardware, runtime, preprocessing, and hyperparameter disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: V3 adds comparisons with Turbal et al. (2025) on Rashomon-set recourse and Kyaw et al. (2026) on Lp-bounded model changes, associated background references, and König et al. (2025) on performative validity. Most related-work material is relocated from v2's Appendix A rather than newly added.

P1.justification: V3 integrates the lengthy related-work appendix into Section 1.1, substantially expands Section 3.1's algorithm explanation and proof sketch, and reorganizes the conclusion. Appendix lettering and citation style also change, materially restructuring the main narrative.

P2.justification: Journal front matter, running headers, typography, and float placement change, including separating Algorithms 1 and 2 across pages. All 60 plot panels across Figures 1–11 retain identical drawing content, and Table 1 retains its structure.

improvement.justification: Correcting Algorithm 2, stating the theorem's solver assumption, providing code/data access information, and qualifying the RBR comparison with fidelity evidence improve precision and usability. These are limited refinements to largely retained experiments and theory. The new Section 3.1 prose incorrectly associates sign changes with |theta[i]| > alpha, contrary to Algorithm 1, but this localized inconsistency does not outweigh the gains.
